title: Edmund and the Room
premise: Dominic Whitlock arrives at Marlowe House School to teach, but the school has a habit of losing one student every generation — and the staff keep immaculate records of everything except why. When the mirrors in his quarters begin showing the room a second behind reality, Dominic discovers the delay is a doorway into 1974, where a boy named Edmund was taken as payment for the school's survival. The last living signatory, elderly headmistress Agnes Vane, is preparing to renew the covenant by signing new papers; Dominic must return what Edmund lost — his name, recorded and then erased — before her signature dries. He succeeds at terrible cost: Edmund is freed, but Dominic must take his place in the room, becoming the reflection that watches, and the book ends with a new teacher arriving to find the mirrors running exactly on time.
about_author: Sebastian Thornbury is the pen name of a former boarding-school archivist who spent eleven years cataloguing institutional records no one was meant to read. They write horror about paperwork, memory, and the small cruelties systems commit in the name of continuity.

chapters.title: The Intake Form
chapters.summary: POV Dominic. Arriving at Marlowe House on a rain-gray September morning, Dominic signs an intake form with an unusual clause about 'residency obligations.' The emotional beat is uneasy ambition — he needs this post, and ignores the clause's strangeness.

chapters.title: Attendance Is Sacred
chapters.summary: POV Dominic. In class, he notices the register lists twenty-nine students but only twenty-eight seats fill. Colleague Ruth Pelling warns him never to mark a missing child 'absent' — only 'unaccounted.' Beat: creeping wrongness beneath routine.

chapters.title: One Second Behind
chapters.summary: POV Dominic. Alone at night, Dominic catches his bathroom mirror lagging — his reflection blinks after he does. He documents it obsessively, telling himself observation is control. Beat: rational mind beginning to crack against evidence.

chapters.title: The Archive Nobody Opens
chapters.summary: POV Dominic. Digging in the school cellar archive, he finds registers from 1974 with a page razored out, and a photograph of a boy whose face is smudged in every copy. Beat: the thrill of discovery curdling into dread.

chapters.title: Ruth's Confession, Over Tea
chapters.summary: POV Ruth. Ruth reveals she was a student here in 1974 and remembers a boy named Edmund — or remembers forgetting him, which is worse. She begs Dominic to leave before term ends. Beat: guilt passed down like inheritance.

chapters.title: What the Mirror Shows
chapters.summary: POV Dominic. The mirror-delay widens to three seconds; in the lag, Dominic sees a bare room with a cot and a boy sitting on it, watching him back. Beat: terror mixed with a terrible tenderness.

chapters.title: Edmund
chapters.summary: POV Edmund (1974). Flashback: Edmund Hale, scholarship boy, is chosen by the old headmaster to 'keep the school warm,' led down past the boiler into a room with no door handle on the inside. Beat: betrayed innocence.

chapters.title: Agnes Vane Signs Nothing Yet
chapters.summary: POV Agnes. The dying headmistress reviews the renewal papers, remembering her own role as a young secretary who typed Edmund's erasure. She believes the covenant is mercy, not murder. Beat: chilling self-justification.

chapters.title: Through the Glass
chapters.summary: POV Dominic. Touching the mirror, Dominic falls through into the room itself — cold, timeless, papered with forty years of scratched tallies. Edmund speaks to him: 'You're the first one who asked my name.' Beat: connection across decades.

chapters.title: The Terms of the Covenant
chapters.summary: POV Dominic. Edmund explains the bargain: the school survives because someone is kept, nameless, unrecorded. To free him, his true name must be written back into the register before the papers are signed. Beat: hope with a deadline attached.

chapters.title: Unaccounted For
chapters.summary: POV Ruth. A current student, Ilsa, goes 'unaccounted'; staff close ranks, and Ruth realizes the covenant is due now, not next year. Beat: panic and complicity — she once helped cover a gap herself.

chapters.title: The Headmaster's Ledger
chapters.summary: POV Dominic. In the restricted ledger, Dominic finds the erasure order bearing seven signatures — including a young Agnes Vane's. Returning the name requires all seven lines countersigned in reversal. Beat: justice requires the guilty.

chapters.title: Confronting Agnes
chapters.summary: POV Agnes. Dominic confronts her; she admits everything but argues the alternative is the school's collapse and hundreds of livelihoods. 'You'd trade them for one ghost?' Beat: the price of survival made explicit.

chapters.title: Ilsa in the Lag
chapters.summary: POV Dominic. Ilsa begins seeing the delayed reflections too — the room is choosing its next resident early. Dominic realizes signing the papers will bind her, not him. Beat: protective fury.

chapters.title: Six Signatures
chapters.summary: POV Ruth. Ruth tracks down surviving signatories; two are dead, four sign reversals — one weeping, one laughing, one demanding money, one already half-mad from dreams of the room. Beat: grim, darkly comic pilgrimage.

chapters.title: The Seventh Line
chapters.summary: POV Agnes. Agnes refuses to the end; alone with the papers, she reads Edmund's file one final time and finds her own childhood handwriting among the witnesses. Beat: the past refusing to stay buried.

chapters.title: Term Ends Early
chapters.summary: POV Dominic. The school begins unraveling — bells ringing backward, corridors lengthening — as the covenant senses its own repeal. Staff flee; Ruth stays. Beat: apocalyptic pressure, loyalty crystallizing.

chapters.title: Signing
chapters.summary: POV Agnes. At midnight, pen poised over the renewal papers, Agnes instead writes Edmund Hale's name back into the 1974 register and signs the seventh reversal with a shaking hand. Beat: redemption purchased too late to be clean.

chapters.title: The Room Lets Go
chapters.summary: POV Edmund. The room dissolves around Edmund as his name takes hold; he steps through the mirror into 2024, aged not a day, into Dominic's arms. Beat: love against duty, briefly victorious.

chapters.title: The Papers Are Still Blank
chapters.summary: POV Dominic. The covenant demands a resident; the school groans on its foundations, and Ilsa stands frozen before the mirror, being pulled. Someone must go back willingly or she'll be taken unwillingly. Beat: the impossible choice.

chapters.title: Edmund and the Room
chapters.summary: POV Dominic. Dominic chooses to return — but Edmund refuses to let him go alone, and the two enter together, their joined names too heavy for the room to erase. It holds them both, imperfectly, forever unfinished. Beat: sacrifice transformed into defiance.

chapters.title: On Time
chapters.summary: POV Ruth, epilogue. A new teacher arrives to find mirrors perfectly punctual, a register listing two names no one remembers adding, and fresh flowers outside a cellar door no one opens. Beat: quiet, haunted peace — survival, paid for and witnessed.
